scope: Finite categorical channels only; no LLM, API, natural-language quality, or practical security claim.
algorithm: Two independently domain-separated seeded samples per unit; equal samples consume no message bit; distinct samples select the next bit. Emit exactly N units including capacity failures.
key_notice: Public demonstration fixture; never a deployment secret.
nonce: First 16 bytes of SHA256(canonical JSON array [experiment_id,profile,N,payload_bytes,replicate]); all predeclared cells, no retry or selection.
payload: First payload_bytes bytes of SHA256(UTF8('seeded-pair-channel-v1:payload:' + decimal replicate)); maximum 32 bytes.
frame: uint16 big-endian payload bit length || payload bytes || first 16 bytes of domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 over authenticated public metadata and length+payload
sampling: HMAC-SHA256 counter blocks, domain separated by nonce, unit index, complete observed prefix and candidate index; unbiased rejection-to-integer weighted categorical sampling
padding: Independent domain-separated HMAC bitstream, used only after the full authenticated frame is consumed
receiver: Separate fresh Python process per attempt; inputs only envelope (stego symbols, nonce, profile, version, units), demonstration key and public implementation/profiles
retention: Every attempt, full stego text, sender completion/capacity counters, decoder result and failure reason retained. No text omitted for insufficient capacity.
metrics: raw capacity bits per emitted unit
sample calls per recovered payload bit
controls: exact rational output-law enumeration on short finite channels
distribution_claim_boundary: Only exact finite-channel identity under ideal independent sampler coins, fixed public output length and all emitted texts. HMAC implementation evidence is not a proof of full cryptographic security. Conditioning on successful payloads can change distributions. No distribution theorem for successful-only texts, explicit nonce envelope, traffic timing, or any LLM.
